prompt: Employers should give their staff at least a 4- week holiday a year to make employees better at their jobs. To what extend do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is often argued that employers should provide their staff with at least four weeks of annual holiday so that workers can perform more effectively. I strongly agree with this view because sufficient rest improves concentration, prevents burnout, and strengthens long-term commitment to the workplace.

The most important reason for granting a four-week holiday is that employees cannot remain productive if they are constantly under pressure. Modern jobs often involve long hours, tight deadlines, and continuous mental effort, all of which can gradually reduce focus and motivation. A meaningful break allows workers to recover physically and emotionally, so they return with clearer thinking and renewed energy. For instance, an accountant who has rested properly after a demanding financial period is likely to make fewer errors and work more efficiently.

Another advantage is that generous annual leave can improve staff loyalty. When employees feel that their employer respects their personal life, they are more likely to feel valued and remain with the company. This benefits businesses because experienced workers understand their roles better and require less training than new recruits. In contrast, organisations that deny adequate holidays may face low morale, frequent absences, and high staff turnover.

Admittedly, some employers may worry that long holidays could disrupt daily operations, especially in small businesses or essential services. However, this problem can be solved through careful scheduling, temporary cover, and fair rotation of leave. Good management should make rest possible without damaging productivity.

In conclusion, I believe that a minimum four-week holiday is not merely a benefit for employees but a practical investment for employers. Well-rested staff are healthier, more focused, and ultimately better at their jobs.
